subject: ventures/home-inspection-report-builder
professional: a working, licensed home inspector (ASHI/InterNACHI-style) who writes 3-4 reports a week and would check first that the report separates safety items up front, that each comment is accurate and defensible, and that the output matches how a client and a buyer's agent read a report

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test` in the venture: 24 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed three outputs by hand with a throwaway script (scratchpad r.mjs): (1) five findings with costs entered as '$1,200'/'1,800.50', 8000/12000, 300/'abc', blank, 50/20 sum by hand to low 1200+8000+0+0+20=9,220 and high 1800.5+12000+300+0+50=14,150.5; summarize() returned 9220 and 14150.5, toText shows '$9,220 to $14,151' (correct rounding). (2) Severity counts by hand safety 2, major 1, minor 1, info 1, priorityCount 3: matched. (3) Severity ordering gfci, gar-door (both safety), roof-worn, int-door, heat-service: matched, with system order as tiebreak. Edge defects found: num() uses Number(), so '0x10' is accepted as 16; a non-numeric high ('abc') with a valid low silently becomes a $0-to-low range (the report prints '$0 to $300' for a figure the inspector never entered); an unknown/corrupt severity on a loaded file silently becomes 'info', downgrading a possible safety item. None affects the normal UI path (number inputs), so 3.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README/page claim by running or reading the path: library of 30 comments across all 10 systems (works, test-enforced); edit wording, severity, notes, cost low/high (works, index.html drawFindings); Save to file and Load (round-trip run in tests and parseImport run by me, works); text download (works); print (print CSS present, not rendered by me). Claim 'print a report sorted with safety and major items first' (index.html line 31) is only partly true: toHtml/toText group by SYSTEM (roof, electrical...) and sort by severity inside each group, so a safety item in Garage prints after minor items in Roof. summarize().sorted (the true severity-first list) is computed but never used by either renderer. JSON-LD featureList claims a 'summary of safety and major items'; the report prints only counts, no list of the priority items (priorityCount is computed and never rendered). No DOM/browser run was possible here, so UI wiring was read, not exercised.
evidence.verification: calc.test.mjs (10 tests), page.test.mjs (8), usage.test.mjs (6): 24 pass in about 0.1s. Seeded five mutations in calc.mjs, reverting each with git checkout (git status clean afterwards): (a) flip `hi < lo` swap to `hi > lo`: 3 tests failed, caught; (b) costHigh sums costLow instead: 1 failed, caught; (c) priority filter drops 'major': 1 failed, caught; (d) change major severity rank 1 to 5 (breaks ordering): 1 failed, caught; (e) import cap `.slice(0,500)` changed to 5: 0 failed, NOT caught (the cap is untested). Gaps: no test of toText/toHtml ordering beyond the summarize call, none for the index.html wiring, none for hex/garbage cost strings.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (163 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, all three test files. Clean pure-function core with no dependencies, escaped HTML output (tested with an XSS payload), try/catch around storage, input caps on import. Defects: summarize().sorted and priorityCount are dead outputs; normalise() silently coerces unknown severity to 'info' and silently reorders/zeros costs with no warning to the user; Download-as-text and Save silently drop untitled findings in text output (normalise+filter in summarize) with no message, while Build shows a message only when all are untitled; counter/Date.now ids are fine. build() calls normalise then toHtml normalises again (harmless double work).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'nothing leaves the browser' (page.test.mjs greps for fetch/XHR/beacon/WebSocket, and no localStorage in index.html; usage.mjs does use localStorage for local counters, which the footer discloses), disclaimer and No warranty text, sponsor link, library does not cite codes (test regex), usage events named on page match record() calls (test). Not backed or off: (1) 'report sorted with safety and major items first' only holds within each system (see completeness); (2) JSON-LD 'summary of safety and major items' is not in the report; (3) llms.txt links to the old duncan-haywood.github.io Pages address, which CLAUDE.md says now only redirects, instead of https://marisstella.app/home-inspection-report-builder/ named in README and VENTURE.yaml (and 'Results are estimates ... not legal, tax, financial advice' boilerplate does not mention that this is a writing aid); (4) README 'Tests: node --test' is correct. The Not decided section and 'not a statement of any standard' limit are honest and present.
evidence.fitness: Walked an inspector's job: fill the header, add findings by system, edit, add cost ranges, build, print or save PDF, download text, save/load JSON. The path is plausible for a tiny report. Gaps an inspector hits in the first hour: no photos (stated), no limitations/not-inspected/scope section, no per-finding location field except free-text note, no inspection-agreement or standards-of-practice scope statement, no way to reorder findings, no custom comment saved to a personal library (a custom finding is lost to the file only), no summary page for the buyer's agent, only 30 comments (a paid tool ships thousands). Free and private is real value for a new inspector, but it is a prototype (VENTURE.yaml stage: prototype) and the hypothesis is untested.
evidence.domain: Compared against ASHI Standards of Practice and InterNACHI SOP report expectations and against Spectora/HomeGauge output norms. Departures: the library is deliberately generic and cites no standard, so wording like 'Receptacles near water ... lacked GFCI protection' is fine but not tied to a defect category the way SOP-style reports are (Safety/Major/Minor/Marginal/Satisfactory are not used; no 'inspected/not inspected/not present' per system); report lacks a limitations and scope section and a summary of the safety items at the top, which is the first thing a client and agent read; severity is per finding with no 'recommend evaluation by a specialist' flag separate from severity; some comments carry judgment a senior inspector would soften (e.g. 'Roof covering ... consistent with advanced age' as a Major defect without remaining-life language). Cost ranges are the inspector's own, which is the safe choice. Reasonable shape for a lead magnet, below a professional report standard.

defects.what: Page claims a report 'sorted with safety and major items first', but both renderers group by system and sort severity only within a system; the globally sorted list (summarize().sorted) is computed and never used, and no priority-items summary is printed despite the JSON-LD featureList claiming one

normalise() silently turns an invalid cost into a plausible range (non-numeric high with low 300 prints '$0 to $300') and an unknown severity into 'info' (a corrupt or hand-edited saved file can downgrade a safety item) with no warning
num() accepts hex and exponent strings ('0x10' becomes 16) because it uses Number()
llms.txt points at the old duncan-haywood.github.io address, not the marisstella.app URL used everywhere else
Import cap of 500 findings is untested (mutation to 5 survived); no tests for toText/toHtml ordering or the page's DOM wiring
Report has no limitations/scope section, no 'not inspected' record and no safety summary at the top, which a professional report requires

verdict: A small, honest, tidy client-side tool whose arithmetic and ordering are right (cost totals, counts and severity order all matched hand computation, and four of five seeded bugs were caught by the 24 passing tests), with correct disclaimers and no data leaving the browser. It does not meet the bar: the headline claim of a safety-first report is true only within each system, the promised priority summary is not rendered, a malformed cost or severity is silently coerced, the library is thin, and the report lacks the scope, limitations and top-of-report safety summary a working inspector expects. Not finished (completeness 2), median 2. Small safe fix: render summarize().sorted (or a 'Priority items' list of safety and major findings) at the top of toHtml and toText, switch llms.txt to the marisstella.app URL, and add tests for ordering and the 500 cap.
